result:
The proposed bound of 1/(3L) is not the tight one.

The derivation uses a crude estimate. It bounds ‖y^k − y^{k−1}‖ ≤ 2a_{k−1} + a_{k−2} (with a_k = λ‖F(y^k)‖) and then applies Young's inequality. This gives the sufficient condition 9μ² < 1. It is the classical Popov-type condition, and the minimization over δ only optimizes this particular proof. It does not show that 1/(3L) is the best possible stepsize bound.

Sharper analyses give larger admissible stepsizes. For monotone operators, stepsizes up to 1/(2L) are known to work. For the pseudo-monotone case, I recall the tight bound as 1/((1+√2)L) = (√2−1)/L ≈ 0.414/L, which is larger than 1/(3L) ≈ 0.333/L. I am recalling this from the literature rather than deriving it here, so I am not fully certain of the exact constant. Either way, 1/(3L) is not tight, so the boxed answer is wrong.

VERDICT: REJECT
